1785b21d52.place: Malabe, Mount Lavinia, Eravur and Sammanthurai
1785b21d52.what_happened: Four people died in four separate road accidents across Sri Lanka on Friday (20), police said. The dead included a 79-year-old woman from Ratmalana and a 23-year-old motorcyclist from Malwatta 02. The crashes were reported in Malabe, Mount Lavinia, Eravur and Sammanthurai.
details: Police said four people were killed in four different road accidents on Friday (20), in Malabe, Mount Lavinia, Eravur and Sammanthurai. The victims included a 79-year-old woman and a 23-year-old motorcyclist.

In Mount Lavinia, a 79-year-old woman from Ratmalana was hit by a car while she was crossing the Galle–Colombo Road. She was badly injured and taken to Kalubowila Hospital, where she died later. Police arrested the car driver.

On the Batticaloa–Trincomalee Road, a 42-year-old motorcyclist from Manampitiya died in a crash involving several vehicles. Police said a lorry heading towards Valaichchenai hit two motorcycles travelling in front of it, then crashed into a car near the Kattupalli Road junction. Both motorcyclists were badly hurt and taken to Eravur Hospital, where one of them died, and the lorry driver was arrested.

On the Kalmunai–Ampara Road, a 23-year-old motorcyclist from Malwatta 02 died after hitting a lorry coming from the opposite direction; the motorcyclist and the pillion rider were taken to Ampara Hospital with serious injuries, and the rider later died of his injuries. Separately, a pedestrian was struck by a motorcycle running along Wanaguru Mawatha from Horahena Junction towards Hokandara Junction; both were badly hurt and taken to Mulleriyawa Hospital, where the pedestrian died, and police said the pedestrian has not yet been identified. The police stations concerned are still investigating all four accidents.
key_facts: Four people died in four separate road accidents across Sri Lanka on Friday (20), police said.
The crashes were reported in Malabe, Mount Lavinia, Eravur and Sammanthurai.
A 79-year-old woman from Ratmalana died at Kalubowila Hospital after a car hit her in Mount Lavinia.
A 42-year-old motorcyclist from Manampitiya died at Eravur Hospital in a Batticaloa–Trincomalee Road pile-up.
A lorry heading to Valaichchenai hit two motorcycles, then a car near Kattupalli Road junction.
A 23-year-old from Malwatta 02 died at Ampara Hospital after hitting an oncoming lorry.
A pedestrian died at Mulleriyawa Hospital after a motorcycle struck them on Wanaguru Mawatha.
The car and lorry drivers were arrested, the pedestrian is unidentified, and investigations continue.
1785b21d52.whats_next: The police stations concerned are continuing investigations into all four accidents, and the identity of the dead pedestrian has not yet been established.
1785b21d52.blurb: Four people died in four separate road crashes across Sri Lanka on Friday, including a 79-year-old woman and two motorcyclists.
1785b21d52.spoken: Police in Sri Lanka are reporting a deadly day on the roads. Four people lost their lives in four separate accidents on Friday the twentieth. The crashes were reported from Malabe, Mount Lavinia, Eravur and Sammanthurai. In Mount Lavinia, a seventy-nine year old woman from Ratmalana was crossing the Galle to Colombo Road when a car struck her. She died at Kalubowila Hospital, and the driver was arrested. On the Batticaloa to Trincomalee Road, a lorry heading towards Valaichchenai ran into two motorcycles and then a car near the Kattupalli Road junction. A forty-two year old rider from Manampitiya died at Eravur Hospital, and the lorry driver was arrested. A twenty-three year old from Malwatta zero two died at Ampara Hospital after hitting an oncoming lorry. And a pedestrian, still unidentified, died at Mulleriyawa Hospital after a motorcycle struck them. Police are investigating all four.

d9d55b2a7c.what_happened: President Donald Trump held a White House press conference on Friday as a test for possible 2028 successors. He asked JD Vance and Marco Rubio to stay still for 90 minutes while he rambled about potholes. Stephen Miller attracted attention as Trump’s favourite offspring.
details: President Donald Trump held a White House press conference on Friday as a test for possible 2028 successors. He asked JD Vance and Marco Rubio to stay still for 90 minutes while he rambled about potholes. The room was crowded, the air‑conditioning hissed, and a sound engineer adjusted the microphone, giving Trump an echo.

Trump referenced his trilateral meeting with China and Russia, likening it to the Yalta conference and noting that the United States, Russia and China control 92% of the world’s nuclear arsenal. He also mentioned his uncle John Trump, an MIT electrical engineer, and claimed a genetic blessing from that background. Rubio then defended the president’s outreach to those leaders, arguing that their combined nuclear power makes regular dialogue essential and dangerous to ignore.

A reporter asked which of the two would make a better president after Trump, and Trump swatted the question away without answering. Vance replied that he would support the president’s Iran policy even though he opposes the war, while Rubio smiled knowingly. The event was described as the first audition for the 2028 election and the article expects further careful positioning in the coming campaign.
d9d55b2a7c.why_it_matters: It is the first audition for the 2028 presidential election.
key_facts: President Donald Trump held a White House press conference on Friday as a 2028 succession audition.
He challenged JD Vance and Marco Rubio to stay still for 90 minutes without reacting.
Stephen Miller sat beside them and attracted attention as Trump’s favourite offspring.
Trump said the United States, Russia and China hold 92% of global nuclear power.
Rubio defended Trump’s engagement with those nuclear powers, calling the idea of avoiding dialogue absurd and dangerous.
Vance pledged to back the president on Iran, and the event is the first 2028 audition.
d9d55b2a7c.whats_next: More needle‑threading is expected in the upcoming campaign.
d9d55b2a7c.blurb: Trump turned a White House press conference into a 2028 succession audition, testing Vance and Rubio while Stephen Miller stole the spotlight.
d9d55b2a7c.spoken: On Friday the president held a White House press conference that was billed as the first audition for the 2028 election. Donald Trump stood at the podium and challenged his potential heirs, JD Vance and Marco Rubio, to stay composed for ninety minutes while he rambled about potholes and other topics. Stephen Miller, his favourite child, sat nearby and drew attention. Trump mentioned that the United States, Russia and China control ninety‑two percent of the world’s nuclear arsenal and referred to his uncle John Trump, an MIT engineer. Rubio defended the president’s outreach to those nuclear powers, while Vance said he would support the president on Iran even though he opposes the war. The event is expected to be followed by more careful positioning in the upcoming campaign.
d9d55b2a7c.subject: 2028 Election

81135dd7ec.what_happened: A Dutch court issued a preliminary injunction on November 20. It blocked BYD from selling its Fang Cheng Bao Ti7 SUV in the European Union. The court found the Ti7 had a similar overall visual impression to the Land Rover Defender and that this infringed design rights.
details: The source is a newswire. BYD, a Chinese electric vehicle giant, got a legal setback. A Dutch court in The Hague issued a preliminary injunction on November 20 after a design rights dispute with British luxury vehicle maker Jaguar Land Rover (JLR).

The court found the BYD Ti7 created a similar overall visual impression to the Land Rover Defender. It cited similarities in overall proportions, rounded shoulders, wheel arches, and window lines. The injunction stopped BYD from importing, manufacturing, offering for sale, selling, storing, or delivering the Ti7 in the European Union.

The restriction applied only to the Ti7 and did not affect BYD’s other vehicles. The Fang Cheng Bao Ti7 is a seven-seat plug-in hybrid SUV from BYD’s Fang Cheng Bao sub-brand. BYD maintained the vehicle was independently designed and did not infringe JLR’s intellectual property rights.

The decision was a legal victory for JLR, which sought to protect the Defender SUV design. But the ruling was a preliminary injunction, not a final judgment after a full trial. The court noted BYD had no concrete plans to bring the Ti7 into the European market at that time, and the case highlights increasing competition as Chinese brands expand.
81135dd7ec.why_it_matters: The case highlights increasing competition between Chinese automakers and established European manufacturers as Chinese brands continue expanding their international presence.
key_facts: BYD got a legal setback from a Dutch court on November 20.
Preliminary injunction blocked BYD Ti7 in the EU.
Court found Ti7 similar to Land Rover Defender.
JLR sought to protect Defender design rights.
BYD said Ti7 was independently designed.
Court said injunction was not final and no EU plans.
Ti7 is a seven-seat plug-in hybrid SUV.
Case highlights Chinese automaker competition.
81135dd7ec.blurb: A Dutch court issued a preliminary injunction blocking BYD’s Ti7 SUV in the EU after finding similarities to the Land Rover Defender.
81135dd7ec.spoken: Here's the scene. A Chinese electric car company called BYD had a legal fight with a British car maker, Jaguar Land Rover. A Dutch court in The Hague gave a ruling on November 20. The court made a preliminary injunction. That blocked BYD from selling its Fang Cheng Bao Ti7 SUV in the European Union. The court said the car had a similar overall visual impression to the Land Rover Defender. It found that was an infringement of design rights. BYD says it was independently designed and does not infringe those rights. JLR says it wanted to protect the Defender design. The order is not a final judgment. The court also said BYD had no concrete plans to bring the Ti7 into the European market then. Here's why it matters. It shows more competition between Chinese automakers and European car makers.
81135dd7ec.subject: BYD Ti7

a4db39a80c.what_happened: Russia launched a major overnight attack on Ukraine, firing ballistic missiles at bridges in Kyiv and railway stations across the country. The strikes hit key crossings in the capital and left at least nine people dead. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called it one of the most massive strikes of the war so far.
details: Russia launched a major overnight attack across Ukraine, targeting bridges in Kyiv and railway stations with ballistic missiles. Key crossings in the capital were hit during the nationwide assault. At least nine people were killed.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky described the strike as one of the most massive of the war so far. The attack came days after Ukraine badly damaged the strategically important Crimean Bridge. Russian President Vladimir Putin had threatened to retaliate for that earlier attack on the bridge.

The Kremlin built the Crimean Bridge to link Russia and the occupied peninsula. The latest strikes took place during a flurry of talks about the war. They also came as the Kremlin pushed back against a US claim that Russia could be open to Western-backed security guarantees for Ukraine.
BBC reporter Sarah Rainsford was in Kyiv after the night of strikes to report on what happened.
key_facts: Russia attacked bridges in Kyiv and railway stations overnight with ballistic missiles.
At least nine people were killed in the nationwide assault on Ukraine.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called it one of the war's most massive strikes.
The attack came days after Ukraine damaged the strategically important Crimean Bridge.
Vladimir Putin had threatened to retaliate for the Crimean Bridge attack.
The Kremlin built the bridge to link Russia and the occupied peninsula.

BBC reporter Sarah Rainsford was in Kyiv after the strikes.
a4db39a80c.blurb: Russia launched a massive overnight missile attack on Kyiv and across Ukraine, killing at least nine people.
a4db39a80c.spoken: Hello and welcome. Russia has launched a major overnight attack on Ukraine, firing ballistic missiles at bridges in Kyiv and railway stations across the country. At least nine people were killed. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called it one of the most massive strikes of the war so far. The assault came just days after Ukraine damaged the strategically important Crimean Bridge, which Russia built to link itself with the occupied peninsula. Vladimir Putin had previously threatened to retaliate for that bridge attack. The strikes also happened while there was a flurry of talks about the war, and as Russia pushed back against a US claim that it might accept Western-backed security guarantees for Ukraine. BBC reporter Sarah Rainsford was in Kyiv after the strikes to bring us the latest.
a4db39a80c.subject: Russia Ukraine war

da8fe7fc70.what_happened: A 6.8 magnitude earthquake hit the Indian Ocean near Banda Aceh on Saturday (21). Sri Lanka’s Department of Meteorology said there is no tsunami threat to the island. The National Tsunami Early Warning Center said the quake happened at about 3:12 PM on November 21, 2026.
details: The earthquake was recorded at a depth of 156 kilometres. Its epicentre was at latitude 8.04° South and longitude 127.57° East. The National Tsunami Early Warning Center gave the time as approximately 3:12 PM on November 21, 2026.

After the quake, the Department of Meteorology issued a No Tsunami Threat Bulletin at 3:30 PM. The bulletin told people in coastal areas around Sri Lanka about the situation. It confirmed that the earthquake does not pose a tsunami threat to Sri Lanka.
The advisory was issued to keep coastal communities informed after the seismic event in the Indian Ocean. The report came from Newswire.

Sri Lanka’s Department of Meteorology says there is no tsunami threat to the island. The National Tsunami Early Warning Center says it happened at about 3:12 PM on November 21, 2026, at a depth of 156 kilometres. 48f549e40a.what_happened: Fausto Isidro "Chapo Isidro" Meza Flores, a Mexican drug lord on the FBI's 10 most wanted list, was arrested after a shoot-out with Mexican authorities. Special forces detained him and seven others in Guasave, Sinaloa on Friday, and the US is now seeking his extradition. Seven suspects and four Mexican army members were killed.
details: Mexican authorities have arrested Fausto Isidro "Chapo Isidro" Meza Flores, a drug lord on the FBI's 10 most wanted list, after a shoot-out. Mexico's defence secretariat said special forces detained him and seven other people in Guasave, in the state of Sinaloa, on Friday. Seven suspects were killed in the operation, and so were four members of the Mexican army who were travelling to reinforce security in Guasave.

The secretariat said the forces used US intelligence on his whereabouts, moved in with what it called "stealth and surprise" and set a perimeter to stop him escaping and reinforcements arriving, but came under attack from gunfire and explosives before entering the property and arresting him. Videos circulating online appear to show helicopters firing streams of bullets towards the ground in Guasave, and people at a baseball stadium fleeing as they hear shooting sounds. Eight people were arrested in total, including his second-in-command, who is also his cousin, and his brother-in-law, the group's financial operator; a grenade launcher, other weapons, drugs and cash were seized, and while Meza Flores, his cousin and his brother-in-law were flown to Mexico City to face prosecution, the other five remained in Sinaloa.

Meza Flores, who is 44, leads the Meza Flores Organisation, also known as the Guasave Cartel, and is thought to have been active in drug trafficking since the 1990s, evading authorities until now by keeping a relatively low profile. He was wanted in Mexico on organised crime charges, and was first charged with drug trafficking in the US in 2012 and charged again in 2019, accused of conspiring to manufacture and distribute large quantities of cocaine, heroin, methamphetamine and marijuana between 2005 and 2019. He was originally a high-ranking member of the Beltrán Leyva Organization, but a split between rival factions led to a surge of violence and prompted him to set up his own cartel by 2013, and his group has since fought what US officials called an "extremely violent turf war" with the Sinaloa Cartel, one of the most powerful trafficking gangs, which operates in the same region.

The FBI accuses him of "flooding the US with fentanyl, cocaine, heroin and other deadly drugs", and the US is seeking his extradition. He was added to the bureau's most-wanted list in 2025, accused of "heinous crimes" including kidnapping, extortion and torture, after Mexican authorities reportedly linked his cartel to 20 million fentanyl pills seized in 2024; then-acting FBI director Brian Driscoll said Meza Flores and his organisation had unleashed a "scourge of illicit drugs" into the US via its southern border with Mexico. Mexico has stepped up efforts to tackle drug-related crime after coming under pressure from US President Donald Trump, who made stemming the flow of drugs across the southern border a key election pledge, while Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum has taken a tougher stance on cartels to resist US intervention on Mexican soil, welcoming closer collaboration but resisting US boots on the ground. The US Consulate General in the city of Hermosillo said it was "monitoring reports of ongoing security operations, armed clashes, road blockades, and vehicle fires that occurred overnight in Ahome, Guamúchil, Guasave, and Navolato" after the arrest, and advised US citizens to stay alert for potential violence and residents to remain sheltered in place.
48f549e40a.why_it_matters: Mexico has stepped up its fight against drug-related crime after pressure from US President Donald Trump, and the arrest removes a man the FBI accuses of flooding the US with fentanyl, cocaine and heroin; the US is now seeking his extradition.

FBI says he flooded the US with fentanyl, cocaine and heroin; US seeks extradition; first charged in 2012.

48f549e40a.whats_next: The US is seeking his extradition. Mexican special forces used American intelligence to find him in Guasave, in Sinaloa, on Friday. They surrounded the property, but came under fire from guns and explosives. c944f8999f.what_happened: The Committee on Ways and Means held discussions on Sri Lanka’s tariff policies and trade agreements. MP Vijesiri Basnayake chaired the meeting, and Acting Director General Somasena Mahadiulwewa briefed the committee.
details: The source is Newswire. The Committee on Ways and Means held discussions. The meeting discussed Sri Lanka’s tariff policies and the progress of ongoing bilateral and multilateral trade agreements.

The meeting was chaired by MP Vijesiri Basnayake. It focused on the current status of trade agreements and measures to advance negotiations. Acting Director General of the Department of Commerce, Somasena Mahadiulwewa, briefed the committee on the country’s trade policies and agreements.

The committee stressed the need to conduct feasibility studies on trade agreements currently under negotiation. It also wanted steps to ensure that discussions progress. Deputy Ministers Chathuranga Abeysinghe and Eranga Weeraratne, along with several MPs, attended the meeting.

4795cded67.what_happened: Minister Nalinda Jayatissa told Parliament that former President Ranil Wickremesinghe spent Rs. 1,010 million on 33 foreign trips during his 26 months in office. By comparison, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake spent Rs. 31.7 million on eight foreign trips over a similar period.
details: Minister Nalinda Jayatissa shared the figures in Parliament on Saturday, November 21. He said former President Ranil Wickremesinghe spent Rs. 1,010 million on 33 foreign trips during his 26 months in office.

According to the minister, 421 people went with Wickremesinghe on those 33 trips. The trips stretched from his visit to the United Kingdom on September 17, 2022, to his visit to India on June 8, 2024.

President Anura Kumara Dissanayake made eight foreign trips in his first 26 months, costing Rs. 31.7 million in total. The minister added that the current President did not claim any extra or combined allowances for those visits.
key_facts: Ranil Wickremesinghe spent Rs. 1,010 million on 33 foreign trips in 26 months.
President Dissanayake spent Rs. 31.7 million on eight trips over a similar period.
Minister Nalinda Jayatissa revealed the figures in Parliament on November 21.

Wickremesinghe's trips ran from a UK visit on Sept 17, 2022 to an India visit on June 8, 2024.

4795cded67.blurb: A minister told Parliament that Ranil Wickremesinghe spent Rs. 1,010 million on foreign trips, far more than President Dissanayake's Rs. 31.7 million.
4795cded67.spoken: Here's a story about how much money two of Sri Lanka's leaders spent on trips abroad. A government minister, Nalinda Jayatissa, told Parliament that former President Ranil Wickremesinghe spent one billion and ten million rupees on thirty-three foreign trips during his twenty-six months in office. That's a lot of globe-trotting, and four hundred and twenty-one people went along with him. By comparison, the current President, Anura Kumara Dissanayake, spent just thirty-one point seven million rupees on eight trips over a similar stretch of time. The minister also pointed out that President Dissanayake didn't claim any extra or combined allowances for those journeys. So the numbers show a big gap between the two leaders' travel spending, and it's now on the public record in Parliament.
4795cded67.subject: Foreign travel costs

dd194f367f.what_happened: Qatari mediators visited Tehran for two hours of talks with Iranian officials on Friday night, as Iran's foreign minister demanded the US meet conditions to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's president called the situation a 'silent economic war,' while the IRGC commander inspected an underground missile facility. The US and Israel attacked Iran on February 28, triggering regional conflict and disrupting global oil shipping.
details: A Qatari delegation traveled to Tehran on Friday night and held two hours of discussions with Iranian officials, Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said. He stated that Iran is in contact with mediators both in person and virtually to see if diplomacy can be given another opportunity. Gharibabadi added that the talks have not yet become formal negotiations, but if they do, technical details of Iran's nuclear programme would be discussed, though Iran insists its enriched uranium must not leave the country.

Gharibabadi also said Iran views the US economic blockade as an act of war and will take any action necessary to break it. US President Donald Trump told Fox News he wants a permanent deal preventing Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon, calling Iranian officials 'very, very difficult' and accusing them of breaking deals. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said the ongoing talks must be given a chance and the blockade lifted rationally, but stressed that discussion on the Strait of Hormuz is pointless unless Iran's demands are met.

Iran's conditions include ending the war on all fronts, unfreezing Iranian assets, lifting oil sanctions, and ending the US counter-blockade of Iranian ports. Araghchi said reopening the strait is not difficult and only requires the US to accept reasonable conditions in accordance with international law. He added there is no solution unless Washington acknowledges its mistakes and fulfills previous commitments. Iran has restricted shipping through the strait, which normally carries about a fifth of the world's oil, since the war began, and the US has imposed a naval blockade on Iranian ports in response.

President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iran is facing a 'silent economic war' tougher than a missile war, blaming a group of bullies, oppressors, and coercers for trying to bring down the country, but noted Iranian businesses have managed market conditions well and the government is working to avoid winter power cuts. Meanwhile, IRGC commander Major-General Ahmad Vahidi toured an underground missile facility with Brigadier General Majid Mousavi, head of the IRGC Aerospace Force, and was briefed on readiness and missile programme developments. The visit follows the Aerospace Force's unveiling of a new underground facility earlier this month displaying ballistic and cruise missiles and launchers.

dd194f367f.spoken: Qatari mediators have arrived in Tehran for talks with Iranian officials, as the country pushes the United States to accept its conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz. The delegation met for two hours on Friday night, and Iran's deputy foreign minister says they're exploring whether diplomacy can get another chance. But Tehran is holding firm: its enriched uranium stays in the country, and it wants the US to end the war on all fronts, unfreeze Iranian assets, lift oil sanctions, and stop the naval blockade on Iranian ports. President Masoud Pezeshkian calls it a silent economic war tougher than any missile attack, while the Revolutionary Guard commander just toured an underground missile facility. The US and Israel struck Iran on February 28, triggering a wider conflict that's disrupted shipping and driven up global oil prices. President Trump says he wants a permanent deal to stop Iran getting a nuclear weapon, but calls Iranian officials very difficult. For now, the talks are not yet formal negotiations, and Iran says discussing the strait is pointless until its demands are met.

e2be825e0d.what_happened: Donald Trump is scheduled to headline his third cryptocurrency gala on Sunday night at his Trump National Golf Club in Sterling, Virginia, rewarding top holders of his $TRUMP meme coin. The event includes meet-and-greets with Floyd Mayweather, Kevin O’Leary, Tristan Thompson and Lior Suchard, and perks are divided by tiers for 185 holders. Democrats accuse Trump of improperly profiting from his crypto ventures and have vowed to investigate conflicts of interest and push legislation banning such activities.
details: Trump is set to headline his third crypto gala on Sunday night at Trump National Golf Club in Sterling, Virginia. The event rewards top holders of his $TRUMP meme coin and includes meet-and-greets with Floyd Mayweather, Kevin O’Leary, Tristan Thompson and Lior Suchard, according to its website. Access is split by tiers for 185 holders: 120 attendees get a Trump fragrance, poster, “commemorative” ticket and “Trump watch”; the top 29 get a VIP reception; the top four get a “TRUMP 18K Gold Watch.”

Democrats say Trump is improperly profiting from his crypto ventures and have criticized him and his family for monetizing his brand through equities and crypto while he is in office. After sweeping wins in the midterms, Democrats vowed to investigate conflicts of interest involving Trump and his personal wealth during his presidency and to push for legislation banning activities such as the meme coin gala dinner. Last month, Adam Schiff and eight other US senators sent a letter saying the dinner and scoring system appeared built to increase investment in $TRUMP and let the president abuse his office to enrich himself.

Since returning to the White House, Trump has made more than $1bn from his crypto businesses, according to financial disclosures released in June. He received more than $500m from World Liberty Financial selling new crypto products and another $600m from sales of souvenir-type “meme” coins stamped with his face; he launched the $Trump meme coin days before his inauguration. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment, while White House spokesperson Anna Kelly told Reuters earlier this year that neither the president nor his family has ever engaged or will ever engage in conflicts of interest and that Trump proudly made the United States the crypto capital of the world through executive actions.

Interest in the $TRUMP dinner has fallen, with contestants’ combined holdings dropping from $148m in May 2025 to $8.6m in this month’s gala; an analysis of blockchain data for Reuters by Public Citizen found more than half of the digital wallets publicly listed on the contest leaderboard for Sunday’s dinner are tied directly to crypto exchanges that bar US-based users, indicating links to foreign nationals. The Trump family’s other crypto-connected equities and ventures have fallen to record lows, and outside investors in their five main crypto and crypto-linked projects have lost more than $5bn, according to a Reuters analysis. The meme coin has earned the Trump family at least $635m, according to the president’s June financial disclosure statement; in total, the Trumps had earned at least $2.3bn through April from their four main crypto ventures, including the meme coin, and the president’s stake in a fifth crypto-linked venture, Trump Media & Technology Group, is worth about $430m.

3663428557.what_happened: WHO chief Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus called for peace after heavy fighting near a hospital in Ituri province disrupted Ebola response efforts. The fighting had been ongoing since yesterday close to where the Ebola outbreak first emerged, forcing health workers and aid partners to shelter in a maternity ward for more than 24 hours. As of November 17, the DRC had 11,613 Ebola cases and 5,678 deaths in its largest and deadliest outbreak.
details: WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus spoke on Sunday about heavy fighting near a hospital in Ituri province. The fighting had been ongoing since yesterday in an area close to where the Ebola outbreak first emerged. It disrupted Ebola response efforts and forced health workers and aid partners to shelter inside a maternity ward for more than 24 hours.

Tedros said the situation puts patients, families and health workers at grave risk. As of November 17, the WHO reported 11,613 Ebola cases and 5,678 deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. This is the largest and deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country.

Ituri and North Kivu in eastern DRC remain the most affected provinces. The WHO said on Saturday that while some areas saw a slight decline in cases, sustained high-level transmission continues overall. The virus spreads through contact with bodily fluids and has spread across the DRC's east and northeast, areas plagued by violence for more than 30 years.

Earlier in November, armed men thought to be linked to an ISIL (ISIS)-affiliated group raided villages in North Kivu and killed dozens of people, forcing patients with confirmed and suspected Ebola infections to flee. The outbreak is also happening amid fighting between government forces and the Rwanda-backed M23 armed group, which has seized key cities in eastern DRC. This makes transport of healthcare resources to remote regions difficult, and the WHO is working to arrange a safe exit for the team and to protect hospital facilities, staff and patients.

2056756415.what_happened: Two fishermen died and a third person was badly hurt after a train hit them in the Cod Bay Fisheries Harbour area of Trincomalee on the night of the 22nd. The three were standing on the railway track when a train going from Trincomalee to Colombo Fort struck them. One died at the scene and another later died in hospital.
details: Police said three people were standing on the railway track when a train travelling from Trincomalee to Colombo Fort hit them in the Cod Bay Fisheries Harbour area of Trincomalee on the night of the 22nd. One person died right at the spot.
The other two were taken to Trincomalee Hospital with serious injuries. One of them later died while being treated, bringing the death toll to two.
The two dead men were both fishermen, aged 48 and 58, from the Matara and Dondra areas. Their bodies were placed at the Trincomalee Hospital mortuary.
The China Bay Police are looking further into what happened.

2056756415.spoken: Here's a sad story from Trincomalee. On the night of the twenty-second, three people were standing on a railway track near the Cod Bay Fisheries Harbour when a train came through. Police say the train was heading from Trincomalee to Colombo Fort, and it struck all three of them. One person died right there at the scene. The other two were rushed to Trincomalee Hospital with serious injuries, but sadly one of them also died while being treated. The two who lost their lives were both fishermen, aged forty-eight and fifty-eight, and they came from the Matara and Dondra areas. Their bodies have been kept at the hospital mortuary. The China Bay Police are now investigating exactly how this happened.

fce8bbdea9.what_happened: Environment Minister Dammika Patabendi denied saying that elephant Kawanthissa died from diarrhoea. He said a daily Sri Lankan Sinhala-language newspaper report was inaccurate. He stressed that only a post-mortem report can determine the real cause of death.
details: Environment Minister Dammika Patabendi issued a statement today (23) denying that he said elephant Kawanthissa died from diarrhoea. He was responding to a report in a daily Sri Lankan Sinhala-language newspaper that claimed the elephant's death was due to diarrhoea.

The minister said he never made that statement and that no one can decide the cause of death based on personal opinion. He said the cause, whether diarrhoea, a gunshot injury, or another reason, must be found through scientific and medical examinations. The final determination will come from the post-mortem report.

He warned that attributing false statements to him could spread misinformation and create public misconceptions. He asked the newspaper to correct the inaccurate report and share his real position with the public. He said the correction should have the same prominence as the original report.

The minister says he never said that. In a statement issued today (23), he explained that the real cause of death can only be confirmed by a post-mortem report. He said it could be diarrhoea, a gunshot injury, or something else, but only scientific and medical tests will tell. He is worried that false quotes spread misinformation and confuse the public. 9379dc90fd.what_happened: The Sri Lanka Human Rights Commission ordered an investigation into damage allegedly caused to Sigiriya Rock during 2017 conservation work, after a petition by Deeman Ananda. The Commission found drilling, cable installation, and use of modern materials had damaged the rock, and directed several government bodies to take prompt action.
details: The Sri Lanka Human Rights Commission issued a determination on October 20 based on a petition filed by Deeman Ananda. The petition alleged that development and conservation work carried out at the Sigiriya World Heritage site in 2017 had destroyed archaeological evidence, including drilling holes, attaching machinery, altering the Lion’s Paw, and removing ancient inscriptions.

An on-site inspection found a cable system installed from the base to the summit to transport materials, with equipment attached to the rock. The rock had been drilled using electrical equipment, and modern mortar and cement were used in conserving ancient mortar. The Commission said the respondents — the Department of Archaeology, Central Cultural Fund, Ministry of Cultural Affairs, and the Sigiriya Project of the Central Cultural Fund — failed to prove the work had proper approval or followed formal procedure.

The Commission concluded the work caused damage to the rock, the most significant natural and cultural feature of Sigiriya, and warned that development without proper procedures could violate cultural and environmental heritage rights. However, the allegation that ancient inscriptions were removed could not be substantiated; the Department of Archaeology said only seven inscriptions had been identified in the area. The Commission stressed the need for a proper mechanism under joint supervision of the Department of Archaeology, the Cultural Triangle, and the National Building Research Organisation for activities of national importance, and made several recommendations to protect archaeological sites and preserve their historical value.
9379dc90fd.why_it_matters: The Commission warned that development without proper procedures could violate rights relating to cultural and environmental heritage.

9379dc90fd.spoken: Good morning. The Sri Lanka Human Rights Commission has ordered a full investigation into damage done to the iconic Sigiriya Rock. This follows a petition by Deeman Ananda, who said conservation work back in 2017 drilled holes into the rock, attached heavy machinery, and even altered the famous Lion’s Paw. Inspectors confirmed a cable system was run from the base to the summit, and modern cement was used on ancient mortar. The Commission found that the Department of Archaeology, the Central Cultural Fund, and other bodies could not prove the work had proper approval. They concluded the rock — the most significant natural and cultural feature of Sigiriya — was damaged, and warned that such unapproved development violates cultural and environmental heritage rights. The claim that ancient inscriptions were removed couldn’t be proven; only seven inscriptions are known in the area. Now the Commission has directed those agencies to act quickly and set up a joint supervision mechanism with the National Building Research Organisation for any future work of national importance.
